How this book matches your exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 11 Mathematics Chapter 1 (Sets) and Chapter 2 (Relations and Functions), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. With Trigonometric Functions (Book 2), these make up Unit I, Sets and Functions — 23 of the 80 theory marks. The paper (3 hours) has MCQs and assertion–reason items, then 2-, 3-, 5-mark and case-based questions; sets and functions appear in every section.

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. Every answer was checked by direct calculation. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme.

Unit 1 of 10: Sets and Their Representation

Key ideas

  • A set is a well-defined collection of objects. "Well-defined" means we can decide whether any object belongs to it. "The five best cricketers" is not a set; "vowels of English" is.
  • Standard sets: N (natural numbers), Z (integers), Q (rationals), R (reals), Z⁺, Q⁺, R⁺.
  • a ∈ A means "a belongs to A"; a ∉ A means it does not.
  • Roster (tabular) form: list elements, e.g. {a, e, i, o, u}. Elements are not repeated; order doesn't matter.
  • Set-builder form: {x : x has property P}, e.g. {x : x is a natural number less than 6} = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

Worked examples

Example 1: Write {x : x is an integer, −2 ≤ x < 3} in roster form. Answer: {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Which is a set? (a) the tall students of a class (b) the prime numbers less than 10 (c) good books (d) difficult chapters. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Write the set of letters of the word "SCHOOL" in roster form. Answer: {S, C, H, O, L}.
  3. (2 marks) Write {1, 4, 9, 16, 25} in set-builder form. Answer: {x : x = n², n ∈ N, n ≤ 5} (2).
  4. (3 marks) Write in roster form: (i) {x : x ∈ N, x² < 20}; (ii) {x : x is a prime factor of 60}; (iii) {x : x ∈ Z, x² = 9}. Answer: {1, 2, 3, 4} (1); {2, 3, 5} (1); {−3, 3} (1).
  5. (3 marks) Explain why "the collection of the 10 most talented writers of India" is not a set, and rewrite it as one. Answer: "most talented" is subjective, not well-defined (1½); e.g. "the writers of India who have won the Jnanpith Award" is well-defined (1½).

Common mistakes

  1. Repeating elements. 2. Ignoring "x ∈ Z" vs "x ∈ N". 3. Ill-defined collections. 4. Including 0 in N. 5. Forgetting negative roots.

Quick recall

  1. N includes 0? 2. Symbol for "belongs to"? 3. Order matters? 4. {x : x ∈ N, x < 1}? 5. Letters of "APPLE"?

Answers: 1) No. 2) ∈. 3) No. 4) ∅. 5) {A, P, L, E}.
